title: fix(ai): avoid retrying conflicting Responses terminal statuses
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Responses sessions start an output-limit continuation when an unfinished tool call is followed by `response.incomplete` and `max_output_tokens`, even though the response explicitly says it completed, failed, or was cancelled.

## User Impact

Sessions no longer make an unnecessary continuation request for contradictory terminal statuses. Genuine output-limit recovery still preserves settled tool results without repeating work, including compatible endpoints that omit `response.status`. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain the canonical terminal stop reason before tool validation replaces the message-level reason with an error, and require that recorded reason to be `length` alongside the existing incomplete-event and output-token-limit evidence. Tool settlement, session retry, and embedded recovery consume the same predicate. Refusal and cancellation precedence remain unchanged; partial arguments never become executable.

Related: #149071. This independent main-targeted fix does not include or depend on that PR’s earlier validation/drain change.

## Evidence

- Original regression proof: 10 managed-transport cases and five real `AgentSession.prompt` cases failed before the fix and passed afterward.
- September 21 refresh: rebased onto main `be3d22b1745917a2c03a1adb999ed51960a3c275`. Resolved the session-table conflict by preserving all landed identity-conflict cases alongside the terminal-status matrix. Range-diff confirms the four-line production change is unchanged; no unrelated CI patches or other PR features were added.
- Fresh focused proof: **228 tests passed** across eight files covering terminal mapping, managed SSE transport, async settlement, loopback WS/SSE continuation and cache behavior, embedded accounting, and session recovery. The loopback tests used `NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost` for fixture servers. The original seven-file run took 37.69 seconds; the newly covered embedded-recovery suite passed all 89 tests. Per-file single-worker costs are recorded below.
- Fresh independent autoreview inspected the final working-tree repair at P0–P2; its sole staging-only finding was resolved by staging the reviewed named fixture data. No code findings remain. `git diff --check` passed. The eight-file changed-check pass and incremental recovery-fixture pass both succeeded, covering all nine changed files.
- Accepted ClawSweeper P2: updated the shared `outputLimitDetails` fixture with the producer’s `stopReason: "length"` and kept negative event/reason cases otherwise coherent. Reproduced five failures locally and in [the previous CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35583441822/job/106281736480); all 89 embedded-recovery tests pass after the repair. Retry budgets and production recovery logic are unchanged.
- Current head: `ebd190517738e135f291cdcc6a71fc4020aa573a`. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35585345477) succeeded, including `openclaw/ci-gate`; the repository watcher reported **GREEN**. [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149242#issuecomment-5683609594) rated this head **platinum hermit (4/6)** with the prior P2 resolved and no remaining actionable findings.
- Additional boundary proof: all nine existing embedded transcript/projection integration tests passed (36.95 seconds wall), including the transport-generated output-limit recovery path.
- Coverage caveat: CodeQL completed **NEUTRAL** with a warning that 16 main-branch scan configurations were absent, so introduced-alert comparison is incomplete. This is an advisory, not a failed CI check.
- Contract checked against [OpenAI SDK 7.15.0 source](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/blob/50eb4b26fc4a70ac355aff5d822e250602faa1e5/src/resources/responses/responses.ts#L1308): `Response.status` is optional and explicit statuses remain authoritative. No authenticated live-provider testing is claimed.

<details>

Each listed file was run separately with `NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1`, measured by `/usr/bin/time`. Wall time includes runner startup and uses the existing compiler cache; no new Gateway boots or sleeps were introduced.
